subject: Can all distributions in Stan be vectorized? Is vectorizing distributions improve speed?

messages.author: 80b903b54c9cf4bd
messages.subject: Can all distributions in Stan be vectorized? Is vectorizing distributions improve speed?
parts:
Hi, I'm a beginner of Stan, and I'm not that confident to vectorize all my distribution statements in Stan, for example, I know 

when mu is a vector, delta is a scalar, 
for(i in 1:N){
y[n]~dnorm(mu,delta)
}

is the same as

y~dnorm(mu, delta)
, is the sense that delta is broadcasted to a vector with the same size as mu, or y, i.e., N.

Can I do the same thing for all the distributions in Stan?
For example,
Vector[N] x;
x~uniform(a,b) # a, b are both scalar


matrix[K,K] sigma[N];
sigma ~ inv_wishart(m, S) # S is a single matrix with the same dim as each element of sigma array, broadcast??

Also, for increment_log_prob(), it can take a vector, suppose I have a vector of log_likelihood log_vec, which way is better:
increment_log_prob(sum(log_vec))
#or
increment_log_prob(log_vec)

Thanks for your patience and hope you don't mind if this question is too simple. I went over the menu 2 times but I'm still not feeling confident when writing programs.

Best!

messages.author: cab04b8f0759c712
messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] Can all distributions in Stan be vectorized? Is vectorizing distributions improve speed?
parts:
On Oct 19, 2015, at 11:27 PM, Jiang Du <jiang...@gmail.com> wrote:

Hi, I'm a beginner of Stan, and I'm not that confident to vectorize all my distribution statements in Stan, for example, I know 

when mu is a vector, delta is a scalar, 
for(i in 1:N){
y[n]~dnorm(mu,delta)
}

is the same as

y~dnorm(mu, delta)
, is the sense that delta is broadcasted to a vector with the same size as mu, or y, i.e., N.
I see you're coming from R. Stan uses "normal" instead of "dnorm."

Can I do the same thing for all the distributions in Stan?
For example,
Vector[N] x;
x~uniform(a,b) # a, b are both scalar


matrix[K,K] sigma[N];
sigma ~ inv_wishart(m, S) # S is a single matrix with the same dim as each element of sigma array, broadcast??

No, we don't have all the multivariate distributions vectorized. The way to determine if it is vectorized is to look at the function signature either in the manual or through rstan (I forget the function to look up Stan functions). 

Plural arguments indicate that it can be given either a scalar or a vector type. For example, "reals" means that argument can accept a real, a row_vector, a vector, or a 1-d array of reals.

Also, for increment_log_prob(), it can take a vector, suppose I have a vector of log_likelihood log_vec, which way is better:
increment_log_prob(sum(log_vec))
#or
increment_log_prob(log_vec)
My guess is the second is better, but this won't impact the overall readability or runtime either way.
Thanks for your patience and hope you don't mind if this question is too simple. I went over the menu 2 times but I'm still not feeling confident when writing programs.

No problem. Good luck!


Best!
